message:
Now I understand the fuzzer input format. It's 3 lines:
1. Source proj string
2. Destination proj string
3. Coordinates (either "x y" text or "BINARY_2D:" or "BINARY_3D:" with binary doubles)

The fuzzer calls `pj_transform(pj_src, pj_dst, 1, 0, &x, &y, &z)` with `point_count=1`.

Now, looking at the `transient_error` array access in `pj_transform`:
```c
if( (srcdefn->ctx->last_errno != 33 /*EDOM*/
     && srcdefn->ctx->last_errno != 34 /*ERANGE*/ )
    && (srcdefn->ctx->last_errno > 0
        || srcdefn->ctx->last_errno < -44 || point_count == 1
        || transient_error[-srcdefn->ctx->last_errno] == 0 ) )
```

Since `point_count == 1` in the fuzzer, the `|| point_count == 1` short-circuits and `transient_error` is NOT accessed in `pj_transform`. But in `pj_datum_transform`, the `CHECK_RETURN` macro does NOT have this `point_count == 1` check:

```c
#define CHECK_RETURN(defn) {if( defn->ctx->last_errno != 0 && (defn->ctx->last_errno > 0 || transient_error[-defn->ctx->last_errno] == 0) ) { if( z_is_temp ) pj_dalloc(z); return defn->ctx->last_errno; }}
```

So if `last_errno` is -50 or lower, `transient_error[-last_errno]` would access `transient_error[50]` or beyond, which is out of bounds.

Now I need to figure out how to trigger an error code of -50 or lower during `pj_datum_transform`. The error codes -52 through -55 are set during projection initialization, not during transformation. But wait - let me check if any projection's `inv` or `fwd` function can set error codes below -49.

Let me look at what error codes can be set during `pj_inv`:

<｜｜DSML｜｜
<parameter=command>grep -rn "pj_ctx_set_errno.*-5[0-9]\|pj_ctx_set_errno.*-6[0-9]" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/proj.4/src/*.c | head -30</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
